    parse string with lat and lon together

    Source: R/parse_llstr.R
    parse_llstr.Rd

    parse string with lat and lon together

    Usage

    parse_llstr(str, format = NULL, order = c("auto", "lat_lon", "lon_lat"))

    Arguments

    str

    (character) string with latitude and longitude, one or more in a vector.

    format

    (character) NULL (the default) or one or more patterns that say how the whole string is written, for example "DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH" for "512839N 0002741W". With several patterns, each string is read with the first pattern that matches it. See the Format and Format examples sections.

    order

    (character) which coordinate comes first in str: "auto" (the default), "lat_lon" or "lon_lat". With "auto", latitude comes first, unless the direction letters only fit longitude first. See the Order section.

    Value

    A data.frame with the columns lat and lon, in decimal degrees, always in this order, whatever the order in str.

    Each part of a string is read on its own: when one part cannot be read, it gives NA with a warning, and the other part is kept. So "abc, -74.5" gives lat NA and lon -74.5. There is one exception: when the latitude is out of range (-90/90) but would be a valid longitude (-180/360), and the string has no direction letter, as in "101.347, 4.9196", the two values are probably swapped. Then both are NA, with a warning that suggests the other order.

    Both values are also NA, with a warning, when a string cannot be cut into two coordinates, does not match any format, or has direction letters that do not fit the order. NA, "" and blank strings give NA without a warning.

    Details

    With format = NULL, each string is cut into two parts, then the latitude part goes through parse_lat() and the longitude part through parse_lon(). The Order section says which part is which. The cut is made at:

    • the comma, when the string has exactly one comma. Spaces around the comma and inside each part are fine: "45.5, -74.5", "45 30 15 S , 74 30 15 W"

    • the only space, when the string has no comma and exactly one space: "45.5 -74.5", "N45.5 W74.5", "45.5N 74.5W". Degrees, minutes and seconds then need a symbol between them, not a space: "45°30'15\"S 74°30'15\"W", "45:30:15 -74:30:15"

    Strings with no separator ("N45.5W74.5"), with two or more commas, or with two or more spaces and no comma ("45 30 74 30") give NA with a warning: use format for them. A dot is never a separator: "45.74" is one number, not two coordinates.

    Each part accepts the formats of parse_lat() and parse_lon():

    • decimal degrees, signed: "45.5, -74.5"

    • a hemisphere letter before or after the number: "N45.5, W74.5", "45.5S, 74.5E"

    • degrees and decimal minutes: "45 30.5, -74 30.5", "N45°30.5', W74°30.5'"

    • degrees, minutes and seconds with any symbols or a dash between them: "45°30'15\", -74°30'15\"", "45:30:15N, 74:30:15W", "45-30-15, 74-30-15"

    • a Unicode minus sign or a dash (U+2212, –) in front of a number is read as a minus sign

    Order

    With order = "auto" (the default), the direction letters N, S, E and W (in upper or lower case) say which coordinate comes first:

    • latitude first, when there is no letter ("45.5, -74.5"), or when the letters fit that ("N45.5, W74.5", "45.5, 74.5W")

    • longitude first, when the letters only fit that: the first part has E or W, or the second part has N or S ("W74.5, N45.5", "74.5W, 45.5", "-74.5, 45.5N"). When only one part has a letter, that part decides.

    • NA for both values, with a warning, when the letters contradict each other: "E45, E30", "N45, N30"

    With order = "lat_lon" or order = "lon_lat", the order is forced. Use it for strings with longitude first and no letters: parse_llstr("-74.5, 45.5", order = "lon_lat"). A string with letters that do not fit the forced order gives NA for both values, with a warning: "N45.5, W74.5" with order = "lon_lat".

    Format

    With format, one pattern describes the whole string: both coordinates and what is between them. For example, "DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH" reads "512839N 0002741W". Each coordinate follows the rules of the Format section of parse_lat(). In addition:

    • The pattern needs exactly two D blocks, one for each coordinate. It is cut in two at the start of the second D block: "DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH" gives "DDMMSSH " and "DDDMMSSH".

    • The two coordinates need no separator: "DDMMSSHDDDMMSSH" reads "512839N0002741W".

    • Each coordinate can have at most one H. An H right between the two coordinates goes with the first one, as in "DDMMSSHDDDMMSSH", unless the first one already has an H. Then it goes with the second one, as in "HD.ddddHDDD.ddd", which reads "N4.9196E101.347".

    • The coordinates follow order. With "lon_lat", the first one is the longitude, as in "DDDMMSSH DDMMSSH". With "auto", the H letters say which one is the latitude, and a pattern without H means latitude first. The number of D letters does not decide.

    • The string is matched as it is: it is not cleaned, and not cut at a comma or a space, as with format = NULL. Spaces at the start and at the end are ignored.

    • Strings that do not match any pattern, or that give NA for one value or both, are listed in one warning. They are not read again with format = NULL.

    • A pattern that cannot work is an error, for example "DDMMSS" (only one D block) or "DDMMSSHH DDDMMSSH" (two H for one coordinate).

    Format examples

    The rules for format are in the Format section above and in the Format section of parse_lat(). order is "auto" when not given.

    strformatorderlatlonWhy
    "512839N 0002741W""DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH"51.4775-0.46139ICAO pair
    "512839N0002741W""DDMMSSHDDDMMSSH"51.4775-0.46139ICAO pair without a separator
    "512839N/0002741W""DDMMSSH/DDDMMSSH"51.4775-0.46139any separator, written as in the string
    "51°28'39\"N 000°27'41\"W""DD°MM'SS\"H DDD°MM'SS\"H"51.4775-0.46139symbols must match exactly
    "4556.98735N 01045.12345W""DDMM.mH DDDMM.mH"45.94979-10.75206NMEA pair
    "4916.45,N,12311.12,W""DDMM.m,H,DDDMM.m,H"49.27417-123.18533NMEA sentence, letters in their own fields
    "N455698735W0104512345""HDDMMmmmmmHDDDMMmmmmm"45.94979-10.75206decimal point not written: exactly 5 decimals
    "N4.9196E101.347""HD.ddddHDDD.ddd"4.9196101.347H in front of each coordinate, no separator
    "4.9196N101.347E""D.dHDDD.dH"4.9196101.347H after each coordinate, no separator
    "-45.5 -074.5""DD.d DDD.d"-45.5-74.5minus signs
    "0002741W 512839N""DDDMMSSH DDMMSSH"51.4775-0.46139longitude first: the letters decide
    "E101.347N4.9196""HDDD.dHD.d"4.9196101.347longitude first, no separator
    "101.347 4.9196""DDD.d D.d""lon_lat"4.9196101.347longitude first, no letters: say so with order
    "101.347 4.9196""DDD.d D.d"NANAno letters, so latitude first, but 101.347 is not a latitude: probably swapped
    "512839N 0002741W""DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH""lon_lat"NANAthe letters do not fit the forced order
    "512839N 0002741N""DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH"NANAtwo latitude letters
    "517539N 0002741W""DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH"NA-0.4613975 minutes: the longitude is kept
    "512839N 1900000W""DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH"51.4775NAlongitude below -180: the latitude is kept
    "51 28 39N 000 27 41W""DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH"NANAdoes not match the pattern
    "51 28 39N 000 27 41W"c("DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH", "DD MM SSH DDD MM SSH")51.4775-0.46139the second pattern matches
    "512839N0002741W"c("DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH", "DDMMSSHDDDMMSSH")51.4775-0.46139the second pattern matches
    "45.5, -74.5"NULL45.5-74.5no letters: latitude first
    "W74.5, N45.5"NULL45.5-74.5longitude first: the letters decide
    "74.5W, 45.5"NULL45.5-74.5only one part has a letter: it decides
    "-74.5, 45.5"NULL"lon_lat"45.5-74.5longitude first, no letters: say so with order
    "N45.5, W74.5"NULL"lon_lat"NANAthe letters do not fit the forced order
    "E45, E30"NULLNANAtwo longitude letters
    "101.347, 4.9196"NULLNANAno letters, so latitude first, but 101.347 is not a latitude: probably swapped
    "abc, -74.5"NULLNA-74.5the latitude cannot be read: the longitude is kept
    "N4.9196E101.347"NULLNANAno separator: use format

    Examples

    parse_llstr("N 04.1683, E 101.5823")
#>      lat      lon
#> 1 4.1683 101.5823
parse_llstr("N04.82344, E101.61320")
#>       lat      lon
#> 1 4.82344 101.6132
parse_llstr("N 04.25164, E 101.70695")
#>       lat     lon
#> 1 4.25164 101.707
parse_llstr("N05.03062, E101.75172")
#>       lat      lon
#> 1 5.03062 101.7517
parse_llstr("N05.03062,E101.75172")
#>       lat      lon
#> 1 5.03062 101.7517
parse_llstr("N4.9196, E101.345")
#>      lat     lon
#> 1 4.9196 101.345
parse_llstr("N4.9196, E101.346")
#>      lat     lon
#> 1 4.9196 101.346
parse_llstr("N4.9196, E101.347")
#>      lat     lon
#> 1 4.9196 101.347
# no comma: the only space is the separator
parse_llstr("N4.9196 E101.347")
#>      lat     lon
#> 1 4.9196 101.347
# signed decimal degrees
parse_llstr("4.9196 -101.347")
#>      lat      lon
#> 1 4.9196 -101.347

# DMS
parse_llstr("N4 51'36\", E101 34'7\"")
#>    lat      lon
#> 1 4.86 101.5686
parse_llstr(c("4 51'36\"S, 101 34'7\"W", "N4 51'36\", E101 34'7\""))
#>     lat       lon
#> 1 -4.86 -101.5686
#> 2  4.86  101.5686
parse_llstr("4:51:36S 101:34:7W")
#>     lat       lon
#> 1 -4.86 -101.5686

# which coordinate comes first (see the Order section)
parse_llstr("W101.347, N4.9196") # the letters say longitude first
#>      lat      lon
#> 1 4.9196 -101.347
parse_llstr("101.347E, 4.9196") # one letter is enough
#>      lat     lon
#> 1 4.9196 101.347
parse_llstr("-101.347, 4.9196", order = "lon_lat") # no letters: say it
#>      lat      lon
#> 1 4.9196 -101.347
# NA and a warning: the letters contradict each other
parse_llstr("E45, E30")
#> Warning: direction letters contradict each other, got: E45, E30
#>   lat lon
#> 1  NA  NA
# NA for both, and a warning: 101.347 is not a latitude, so the values
# are probably swapped
parse_llstr("101.347, 4.9196")
#> Warning: not within -90/90 range, got: 101.347
#>   check that you did not invert lon and lat
#> Warning: latitude out of range but valid as a longitude, so longitude may come first: try order = "lon_lat", got: 101.347, 4.9196
#>   lat lon
#> 1  NA  NA
parse_llstr("101.347, 4.9196", order = "lon_lat")
#>      lat     lon
#> 1 4.9196 101.347
# one part cannot be read: the other one is kept
parse_llstr("abc, -74.5")
#> Warning: no digits detected, got: abc
#>   lat   lon
#> 1  NA -74.5

# with format: one pattern for the whole string (see the Format section)
parse_llstr("512839N 0002741W", format = "DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH") # ICAO
#>       lat        lon
#> 1 51.4775 -0.4613889
parse_llstr("512839N0002741W", format = "DDMMSSHDDDMMSSH") # no separator
#>       lat        lon
#> 1 51.4775 -0.4613889
parse_llstr("4916.45,N,12311.12,W", format = "DDMM.m,H,DDDMM.m,H") # NMEA
#>        lat       lon
#> 1 49.27417 -123.1853
parse_llstr("N4.9196E101.347", format = "HD.ddddHDDD.ddd")
#>      lat     lon
#> 1 4.9196 101.347
# longitude first: the letters decide
parse_llstr("0002741W 512839N", format = "DDDMMSSH DDMMSSH")
#>       lat        lon
#> 1 51.4775 -0.4613889
# longitude first, without letters
parse_llstr("101.347 4.9196", format = "DDD.d D.d", order = "lon_lat")
#>      lat     lon
#> 1 4.9196 101.347
# several formats, tried in order for each string
parse_llstr(
  c("512839N 0002741W", "512839N0002741W", "51 28 39N 000 27 41W"),
  format = c("DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH", "DDMMSSHDDDMMSSH", "DD MM SSH DDD MM SSH")
)
#>       lat        lon
#> 1 51.4775 -0.4613889
#> 2 51.4775 -0.4613889
#> 3 51.4775 -0.4613889
# NA and one warning: 75 minutes (the longitude is kept), and two
# latitude letters
parse_llstr(
  c("517539N 0002741W", "512839N 0002741N"),
  format = "DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH"
)
#> Warning: NA for 2 value(s) that could not be read with `format`:
#>   "517539N 0002741W": latitude: minutes or seconds not within 0/60 range
#>   "512839N 0002741N": direction letters contradict each other
#>   lat        lon
#> 1  NA -0.4613889
#> 2  NA         NA
# without format, a string with no separator gives NA and a warning
parse_llstr("N4.9196E101.347")
#> Warning: could not split into latitude and longitude, got: N4.9196E101.347
#>   lat lon
#> 1  NA  NA

# add both columns with one call, picking them by name
df <- data.frame(x = c("N4.9196, E101.347", "4.9196 -101.347"))
cbind(df, parse_llstr(str = df[["x"]])[c("lat", "lon")])
#>                   x    lat      lon
#> 1 N4.9196, E101.347 4.9196  101.347
#> 2   4.9196 -101.347 4.9196 -101.347
# dplyr:      df |> dplyr::mutate(parse_llstr(str = x)[c("lat", "lon")])
# data.table: dt[, c("lat", "lon") := parse_llstr(str = x)[c("lat", "lon")]]
